species.changed: Replaced the generic arched body with Digital Life’s distinct Southern right-whale sculpt, original atlas and retained skeleton/source clip. Legacy material compatibility restores the source diffuse maps; source image bytes and binary geometry/rig/animation are unchanged.
species.residual: Callosities and scratches remain an artist pattern rather than a redetermined animal; some pale patches are flat and smooth. Creator drone-derived proportions are source-reported, not a new archive morphometric fit. Tissue optics, full filtration and measured swimming remain unresolved.
species.comparison: The whole Hugo Hulsberg breach photograph supports external head/callosity and gross-body comparison but obscures the submerged body. Separate Digital Life provenance reports drone widths/heights at5% length increments plus anatomical sculpting. No North Atlantic or North Pacific right-whale source is substituted.

species.name: Kogia breviceps
species.changed: Replaced the generic rounded template with the distinct CARI’MAM pygmy sperm-whale sculpt and original atlas: blunt shark-like head, small underslung jaw region, compact flippers, low posterior fin, false-gill pigment and a textured countershaded skin.
species.residual: False-gill detail, lower-jaw margins, eyes, surface grain, source colour and proportions remain selected artist features. The rare live profile photograph shows only the surfaced back/head; it cannot validate the concealed appendages. Suction feeding, full jaw anatomy, discharge and physiology remain unfinished.
species.comparison: The retained whole Charlotte Kirchner live image is restricted surface evidence. Separate FAO and NOAA species anatomy distinguishes the low posterior fin and false-gill mark from true gills and from the taller central-fin dwarf sperm whale. The dwarf model is not replaced by this K.breviceps body.

species.name: Ziphius cavirostris
species.changed: Replaced the generic beaked template with CARI’MAM’s distinct Cuvier sculpt and original scarred atlas: goose-like short beak/forehead, pectoral recess regions, compact flippers, posterior fin and selected swept flukes. Display orientation is corrected to the other main-viewer bodies.
species.residual: Pale head and scratches do not independently establish sex/age. Separate erupted apical teeth are not resolved in this artist model, and the record now states that limit. The selected source flukes have a shallow medial indentation. Some scars remain conspicuous/baked; cross-sections, wet optics, suction mechanics and full deep-dive motion are unmeasured.
species.comparison: The retained whole Charlotte Kirchner surface photo shows a brown individual and limited back/head. It is not a same-individual fit to the artist’s pale scarred exterior. NOAA and FAO descriptions provide separate short-beak/concave-forehead and fin context.
